This barley plot is small, only a quarter hectare, but it feeds my family so I take care of it. I will get some DAP and urea from the cooperative if it arrives in time — barley needs feeding to give a good harvest, but I cannot afford a heavy dose. I also spread manure from my oxen and small ruminants on this plot every year because it keeps the soil strong. For seed, I save my own barley from last harvest like my neighbors do; improved barley seed is hard to find here and the local variety is well-suited to our cool weather. I depend on the meher rains, no irrigation, and my wife and older children help me through weeding and harvest.
